key_insight: DemoPSD improves on-policy self-distillation by modulating how much the student trusts the teacher based on disagreement, reducing overfitting to narrow patterns while preserving useful guidance for reasoning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a core weakness of on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: dense token-level teacher supervision can suppress exploration, overfit to in-domain data, and hurt cross-domain generalization.
method: Use a disagreement signal between teacher and student to determine when teacher supervision should be strong or weakened.
Replace uniform dense token-level guidance with disagreement-modulated distillation, so the student can explore more when the teacher is likely overconfident or misaligned.
Train the model in an on-policy self-distillation setup that keeps the benefits of self-teaching while reducing harmful imitation pressure.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more robust way to train reasoning models that generalize better across tasks and domains. It is especially relevant when standard distillation improves training loss but degrades exploration and real-world transfer.
